params.body:
Counterpart of abovebeyond-ai/elixir#170. Elixir judges the Deployed measurement itself; this makes Portal render that verdict instead of computing its own.

- `App\Support\Level` (now, week, month, background, ok; the same words and ranks as Elixir's) and `App\Support\Verdicts` (reads `elixirData[key].verdicts`; null means "Elixir did not judge", never ok).
- The Deployed card renders Elixir's word and the reason with the threshold that fired ("Judged" line). A row without verdicts (written before today) still falls back on the old rule; that fallback goes in a follow-up once every row carries a verdict.
- The fleet brief: `verdict` per measurement carries `source` (elixir or portal) and `facets` (`{facet, level, threshold, reason}`); the catalogue carries `judgements` per key; tasks carry `facet`. Staging reads Elixir's verdicts directly (no cards there).
- English identifiers where this touched Dutch ones: `meting` → `measurementKey` on blocks and in the views, `MEETSLEUTEL` → `MEASUREMENT_KEYS`; the severity constants are now the ranks of `Level`.
- `docs/fleet-brief.md` and `docs/elixir-architecture.md` (the layers) updated.

Tests: `DeployedCardTest` (Elixir's word wins even where the old rule would differ; a row without a verdict keeps the old rule; the helper never invents ok), `FleetBriefTest`. Suite green except `BuildStampTest` in this worktree; PHPStan green.

Proposed through the control gateway under #agent-workbench.
params.title: Portal renders Elixir's verdict: Level, Verdicts, and Deployed as the first card
